title: Eighth Word Comparing The Two Travelers And The Quranic Judgment

questions.question: What is the biggest difference between the two travelers at the start of this passage?
questions.answer: One is full of fear and misery, while the other is welcomed into a beautiful garden.

questions.question: How does the unhappy traveler feel about what is going to happen to him?
questions.answer: He stays scared and expects something terrible.

questions.question: How does the fortunate traveler look at the strange things around him?
questions.answer: He sees them as a meaningful and enjoyable lesson.

questions.question: What kinds of feelings fill the fortunate traveler?
questions.answer: He has hope, longing, and a feeling that he belongs.

questions.question: How does the miserable traveler see himself?
questions.answer: He sees himself like a trapped prisoner surrounded by danger.

questions.question: How is the fortunate traveler treated instead?
questions.answer: He is treated like a respected guest among friendly servants.

questions.question: What mistake does the unhappy traveler make with the fruit?
questions.answer: He keeps eating it for pleasure even though it is harmful.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the right way to deal with those fruits?
questions.answer: A person may taste them to understand and seek what they point to, but should not greedily consume them.

questions.question: What does the fortunate traveler do when he tastes the fruit?
questions.answer: He understands its purpose and waits patiently instead of rushing to eat more.

questions.question: How does the unhappy traveler harm himself with his thinking?
questions.answer: He turns something clear and real into dark fear and a false nightmare.

questions.question: What example is given to show how a person can wrong himself?
questions.answer: A man at a nice summer gathering gets drunk, imagines he is in a terrible place, and starts crying out.

questions.question: Why does that drunken man not deserve pity in the example?
questions.answer: Because he caused his own misery and wrongly judged his friends and surroundings.

questions.question: Which brother is compared to that drunken man?
questions.answer: The unfortunate brother.

questions.question: Why does the fortunate brother deserve mercy?
questions.answer: Because he recognizes the truth as good and shows respect to the One who owns that truth.

questions.question: What lesson from the Qur’an is explained by this comparison?
questions.answer: Harm comes from a person’s own wrong choices, while good comes from Allah.

questions.question: What qualities help the fortunate brother receive blessings and happiness?
questions.answer: Good intention, good will, good character, and good thoughts.

questions.question: What has the first brother’s lower self prepared for him?
questions.answer: It has made a kind of hell for him.

questions.question: Where is the traveler on the left road headed in his fear?
questions.answer: He expects to end up in the dragon’s mouth.

questions.question: What is the condition of the place the fortunate traveler is invited into?
questions.answer: It is a rich and beautiful garden full of fruit.

questions.question: What is pounding in the unfortunate traveler’s heart?
questions.answer: Severe fear and distress.

questions.question: What kind of fear does the fortunate traveler have?
questions.answer: He has a gentle fear joined with love and understanding.

questions.question: What three painful feelings trouble the unfortunate traveler?
questions.answer: He feels isolated, hopeless, and lonely.

questions.question: What three hopeful feelings strengthen the fortunate traveler?
questions.answer: He feels hope, eager desire, and closeness.

questions.question: How do the two travelers differ in the way they see the creatures around them?
questions.answer: One sees attacking wild animals, while the other sees friendly servants of a generous host.

questions.question: Why are the fruits not meant to be eaten greedily?
questions.answer: They are only signs and samples meant to guide a person to something greater.

questions.question: What does the fortunate traveler understand after tasting the fruits?
questions.answer: He understands their meaning and is willing to wait.

questions.question: What does the passage say the unfortunate traveler does to a bright reality?
questions.answer: He changes it in his mind into a dark, crushing fear.

questions.question: In the example of the banquet, what caused the man’s confusion?
questions.answer: He made himself drunk with filthy intoxicants.

questions.question: What false ideas does that man imagine after becoming drunk?
questions.answer: He thinks he is freezing, hungry, alone, and surrounded by dangerous animals.

questions.question: How is insulting his friends part of his wrongdoing?
questions.answer: He imagines good companions to be savage creatures.

questions.question: What does the fortunate brother do differently from the unfortunate one?
questions.answer: He sees what is true instead of turning it into a lie in his mind.

questions.question: Why is seeing the truth properly a form of respect?
questions.answer: Because it honors the One who made that truth.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the source of evil?
questions.answer: Evil begins from a person’s own self.

questions.question: What result comes from the second brother’s good thoughts and character?
questions.answer: He receives many blessings, real happiness, and shining virtue.

questions.question: Compare the ending direction of the two travelers in this passage.
questions.answer: The unhappy one moves toward terror, while the fortunate one is brought toward beauty and welcome.

questions.question: How does the unfortunate traveler spend his time emotionally?
questions.answer: He keeps shaking with fear.

questions.question: What does the fortunate traveler do with the unusual things he sees?
questions.answer: He studies them and benefits from them.

questions.question: What makes the fortunate traveler’s fear different from the other one’s fear?
questions.answer: His fear is mixed with love, learning, and peace instead of despair.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the unfortunate traveler’s inner condition?
questions.answer: He is in deep suffering because he feels alone and without hope.

questions.question: What picture is given of the fortunate traveler’s relationship to the place he is in?
questions.answer: He belongs there like an honored visitor.

questions.question: How does overeating the fruit increase the unfortunate traveler’s suffering?
questions.answer: He chases short pleasure that actually brings him more pain.

questions.question: What permission is given about the fruit?
questions.answer: Only enough to sample and understand.

questions.question: What is denied about the fruit?
questions.answer: A person is not allowed to gobble it up like an animal.

questions.question: What personal fault causes the unfortunate traveler to wrong himself?
questions.answer: He lacks clear judgment.

questions.question: What does he do to something clear like daylight?
questions.answer: He covers it in darkness through his mistaken thinking.

questions.question: What season and setting are used in the example of the banquet?
questions.answer: It is a beautiful summer meal in a lovely garden with friends.

questions.question: After ruining his thinking, what does the man in the example start doing?
questions.answer: He cries out and acts as if he is in danger.

questions.question: Why is the unfortunate brother compared to that man?
questions.answer: Because both create misery for themselves by seeing things falsely.

questions.question: What is special about the fortunate brother’s view of reality?
questions.answer: He recognizes its goodness and beauty.

questions.question: According to the Qur’anic teaching quoted here, where does good come from?
questions.answer: It comes from Allah.

questions.question: What four good qualities are named as reasons for the second brother’s success?
questions.answer: Good intention, good will, good character, and good thoughts.

questions.question: What is one traveler waiting for with dread, and what is the other invited to?
questions.answer: One fears being swallowed by the dragon, and the other is welcomed into a rich garden.

questions.question: How is the unfortunate traveler’s fear described?
questions.answer: It is harsh, heavy, and painful.

questions.question: How does the fortunate traveler use what he sees around him?
questions.answer: He treats it like a lesson that brings understanding.

questions.question: What does the fortunate traveler feel along with fear?
questions.answer: He also feels love and knowledge.

questions.question: What conditions make life bitter for the unfortunate traveler?
questions.answer: Despair, loneliness, and inner torment.

questions.question: What makes life sweet for the fortunate traveler?
questions.answer: Hope, longing, and feeling connected.

questions.question: What is the difference between being a prisoner and being an honored guest in this passage?
questions.answer: The prisoner feels attacked and trapped, while the guest is welcomed and cared for.

questions.question: Why are the fruits dangerous for the unhappy traveler?
questions.answer: He uses them in the wrong way and seeks only quick pleasure.

questions.question: What wise action does the fortunate traveler take with the fruits?
questions.answer: He tastes, understands, waits, and enjoys being patient.

questions.question: What does the passage say the unhappy traveler deserves because of his false thinking?
questions.answer: He does not deserve pity.

questions.question: Why does he have no right to complain?
questions.answer: Because he brought the darkness on himself.

questions.question: What does the drunk man in the example wrongly believe about his friends?
questions.answer: He thinks they are like wild beasts.

questions.question: How does that example help explain the unfortunate brother?
questions.answer: It shows that his suffering comes from his own bad way of seeing things.

questions.question: What does the fortunate brother recognize about the truth?
questions.answer: He sees that it is good.

questions.question: What does respecting the truth lead him to deserve?
questions.answer: Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: What does the quoted Qur’anic rule say about evil and good?
questions.answer: Harm comes from oneself, and good comes from Allah.

questions.question: What has the first brother’s lower self built for him, and what has the second brother’s goodness opened for him?
questions.answer: The first has made a kind of hell, and the second has opened the way to blessings, happiness, and virtue.

questions.question: In this passage, how are the two brothers shown to end up very differently?
questions.answer: One lives in terror and misery, while the other receives welcome, joy, and peace.

questions.question: What is the unhappy traveler always expecting?
questions.answer: He expects a dreadful end.

questions.question: What does the fortunate traveler gain from looking carefully at strange events?
questions.answer: He gains a pleasant lesson and loving understanding.

questions.question: What emotions trap the unfortunate traveler?
questions.answer: Fear, sadness, hopelessness, and loneliness.

questions.question: What emotions lift up the fortunate traveler?
questions.answer: Hope, desire for good, and a sense of closeness.

questions.question: How do the two travelers differ in status?
questions.answer: One feels like a captive under attack, and the other is treated like an honored visitor.

questions.question: What is wrong with the unhappy traveler’s way of eating the fruit?
questions.answer: He acts greedily and thoughtlessly.

questions.question: What is the purpose of tasting the fruit only a little?
questions.answer: It helps a person understand and seek the real gift behind it.

questions.question: How does waiting become a good thing for the fortunate traveler?
questions.answer: He enjoys patience because he understands there is something better ahead.

questions.question: What is the unhappy traveler doing to himself besides eating wrongly?
questions.answer: He is hurting himself by misreading reality.

questions.question: What kind of reality is he misreading?
questions.answer: One that is actually clear and bright.

questions.question: In the example, what kind of place is the man really in?
questions.answer: He is really in a pleasant gathering with friends.

questions.question: What makes his cries foolish?
questions.answer: His fear comes from his own drunken confusion, not from real danger.

questions.question: Why is the unfortunate brother said to be like that man?
questions.answer: Because he turns a good reality into a nightmare through his own bad state.

questions.question: How does the fortunate brother act toward the truth’s owner?
questions.answer: He shows respect.

questions.question: What main message is taught by the line about evil and good?
questions.answer: A person’s own wrong self causes evil, but Allah is the source of good.

questions.question: What good results come to the second brother because of his inner goodness?
questions.answer: He receives blessings, true happiness, prosperity, and beautiful virtue.

questions.question: What scene shows the difference between the two travelers most clearly?
questions.answer: One is terrified of destruction, while the other is welcomed into a fruitful and lovely garden.

questions.question: What is happening inside the unfortunate traveler’s heart?
questions.answer: It is beating under heavy fear and pain.

questions.question: What is the fortunate traveler doing instead of panicking?
questions.answer: He is observing and learning from what he sees.

questions.question: What kind of knowledge does the fortunate traveler gain?
questions.answer: He gains understanding joined with love.

questions.question: How is the unfortunate traveler’s life described emotionally?
questions.answer: It is full of torment, emptiness, and hopeless isolation.

questions.question: How is the fortunate traveler’s life described emotionally?
questions.answer: It is filled with hope, joyful expectation, and belonging.

questions.question: What difference is there between their relationships to the beings around them?
questions.answer: One feels threatened by beasts, but the other is at ease with servants of a generous master.

questions.question: Why does the unhappy traveler’s pleasure from the fruits not really help him?
questions.answer: The fruits seem sweet at first, but they actually harm him.

questions.question: What does the fortunate traveler understand about the fruits that changes his behavior?
questions.answer: He understands they point beyond themselves, so he waits instead of grabbing more.

questions.question: What does the passage call the unhappy traveler’s false way of seeing things?
questions.answer: It is described as a dark and hell-like delusion.

questions.question: What does the example of the drunk man teach about self-caused suffering?
questions.answer: A person can make himself miserable by ruining his judgment.

questions.question: How does the drunk man treat good people in his imagination?
questions.answer: He unfairly sees them as dangerous creatures.

questions.question: Why does the passage say such a person should not be pitied?
questions.answer: Because he brought the trouble on himself.

questions.question: What does the fortunate brother do that is opposite to this?
questions.answer: He accepts the truth as it really is.

questions.question: Why does that make him worthy of mercy?
questions.answer: Because he honors the goodness and beauty placed in reality.

questions.question: What has the first brother’s lower self produced for him?
questions.answer: It has produced something like a private hell.

questions.question: What has the second brother’s good intention and good thoughts allowed him to receive?
questions.answer: They have allowed him to receive abundant gifts, real happiness, success, and noble character.
